subject: Quick rate scan for pilot — 1M token input/output and model roster
messages:
From: Alyssa Greene <alyssa@medlytics.ai>
To: ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: MedLytics Procurement <procurement@medlytics.ai>
Date: 2028-02-15T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Rate check for pilot — per 1M token IO + model list

Hi Ben,

Thanks for taking a look — we’re scoping a short pilot (6–8 weeks) to evaluate hosted inference for clinical-notes summarization. Procurement asked me to get a baseline per-1M token rate split by input vs output, and a list of the small/medium model variants you support on the hosted API (we care about Llama-family open models and any Redwood-verified alternatives).

High-level ask: can you send your standard hosted IO pricing (input / output per 1M tokens), any note on streaming vs non-streaming pricing differences, and a one-line model roster (model name, typical latency tier) we can use in our cost model? If there are common pilot discounts or short-term credits for early-stage pilots, please note those too.

Appreciate a quick reply — we’re trying to lock assumptions for a financing review on Friday.

Best,
Alyssa Greene
Head of Product
MedLytics
[attachment: medlytics_pilot_scope.docx (DOCX, 85 KB)]
From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: Alyssa Greene <alyssa@medlytics.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-02-15T11:04:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Rate check for pilot — per 1M token IO + model list

Hi Alyssa — thanks for the clear ask and the scope doc. Quick answers below; I’ve attached a short one-pager and a sample cost calc.

Baseline hosted IO pricing (standard, non-committed):
- Input tokens: $0.50 per 1M tokens
- Output tokens: $1.00 per 1M tokens

Notes:
- Streaming responses are billed at the same IO rates; we do not apply a separate streaming surcharge.
- For models with higher compute (large Llama variants & some verified encoder-decoder models) plan-level multipliers may apply — I’ve called those out in the attached rate sheet where relevant.

Model roster (short):
- redwood-llama-13b (open, medium latency)
- redwood-llama-7b (open, low latency)
- redwood-llama-30b-q4 (quantized, medium-high latency)
- redwood-tuned-instruct (verified, medium latency)

What I can offer for pilot customers:
- One-time $2,500 pilot credit for trials up to 2M total tokens processed in the pilot window.
- For pilot commitments that convert to a 12-month reserved path, we commonly offer a 10–20% discount depending on committed spend.

I’m looping in Marissa for any model-specific notes (latency / footprint) and to confirm the rate-sheet attachment is the latest. If you want a formal quote or an estimated cost table for the sample workload in your doc, tell me the target daily requests and avg prompt/response length and I’ll run numbers.

Thanks —
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Rate check for pilot — per 1M token IO + model list

Thanks Ben — that’s helpful. Two quick clarifications: 1) when you say 'input' tokens, does that include any system prompts or instruction tokens (i.e., full request envelope)? 2) Our CFO is specifically asking whether the output rate is symmetric for streaming partial responses (we have some streaming UI cases).

Also — assuming we go with a 12-month reservation after pilot, can you give a ballpark for the tier thresholds you use to qualify for 15% vs 20% committed discounts (so we can set expectations internally)? Finally, any difference in rate treatment for embeddings calls vs generation (we may evaluate both)?

—Alyssa
From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: Alyssa Greene <alyssa@medlytics.ai>
Cc: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-02-16T15:04:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Rate check for pilot — per 1M token IO + model list

Alyssa — answers inline and looping in Hannah for discount approval. Marissa, quick note on the models if you see anything to add.

1) Input token definition: we bill for the entire request envelope (system + user + any tool calls). So include system prompts in your estimate.

2) Streaming: output tokens are billed the same whether delivered streaming or non-streaming; partials count as output tokens as they’re emitted. No separate streaming pricing.

3) Committed discount thresholds (ballpark):
- Tier A (15%): $250k annual committed spend
- Tier B (20%): $500k+ annual committed spend

4) Embeddings vs generation: embeddings are billed as a separate SKU at $0.40 per 1M embedding tokens for standard models; off-the-shelf embedding models have different performance characteristics — Marissa can advise on which model in the roster we recommend for vector pipelines.

Hannah — if those discount bands look OK, can you confirm a standard 15% for $250k ARR and 20% at $500k ARR for hosted (subject to contract)? If there’s a different preferred cadence (e.g., commit by spend or by GPU-hours) happy to adjust.

Thanks,
Ben
